$comment: Checkable mirror of the return blocks the skills declare in prose. The prose of each declaring file stays the normative schema; on divergence the prose holds and this file is updated to match. Read by hand-written checks (readFile + JSON.parse, no dependencies) and by humans writing nodes. Method only: no guest values, no machine paths.

decision-doc.note: The fields between `stage_why` and `decisions` are the ones the stage turns on, and `direction` is null when nothing proposes one. Which of them the stage admits — a technical stage executes the owner's direction and rests on verified premises, a strategic one carries no premises of a direction nobody chose — is not expressible as an enum: it is SHAPES['decision-doc'] of architect/architect.mjs. The same shape holds `crossed_stages` to what the block actually carries, so the crossing of the two stages cannot go undeclared, and admits `closed-elsewhere` only with the `closed_by` that answers a precedent the strategic stage already closed.

blueprint.note: The same object stands in § Handoff of 2. blueprint.md, its seat on disk. The rules the prose adds — every task with a non-empty check and red_if, cases rows with input and expected, consumers as strings — are SHAPES.blueprint of architect/architect.mjs.

execute.note: The same object stands in § Handoff of 4. review-notes.md, its seat on disk. The rules the prose adds — a red proof with a non-zero exit and its output, a count with a reason for every hit left, each of the four preflight steps present — are SHAPES.execute of architect/architect.mjs. The evidence is never remeasured against the disk downstream: the maps the brief built are the last measurement.

applier.note: Every item of the four lists carries `finding_id`, and every finding handed over has exactly one outcome: the `block` question checks it against the `finding_ids` passed beside the block. `to_confirm.class` enumerates every discipline a round-1 finder can hand over — `bug`, `arch`, `perf`, `dead` — plus `test-coverage`, the class the closing round on tests adds.

code-review-outcome.note: The block of the bug-only cycle: the shape of § review-outcome minus the fields a bug-only cycle, stopping at the report, does not produce — `disciplines_round_1` and `independence` (one discipline, `bug`, always), `commit` and `commit_sha` (the cycle never commits), `blocking`, `coverage` and `report`. No `question` feeds it: the cycle stops at the report and hands the block to its caller, so this entry is the map of a shape the skill declares in prose, not a check any program runs — the prose of `skills/code-review/SKILL.md` stays the normative schema.

research.note: No JSON block: returns only the reordered file path.

new-feature.note: No JSON block of its own: reports the ship-feature block verbatim; its status is that block's status.

architect.producer: skills/ship-feature/SKILL.md § The evaluator (architect-internal, no producer file)
architect.note: The effective domain of `verdict` depends on `question`: this enum is the union of the eleven domains, one per question — decision, closing, unblock, propagation, resumption, order, round, layers, block, pool, reconcile — and `verdict` is `null` when the question does not apply, that is `propagation` on a block that came back. `remaining` and `resume_from` are filled by `order` and `resumption` alone; `slot` by `pool` alone, the number of the pool worktree to reuse or create; `retry` and `fallback` by `propagation` alone; `readings` by the ambiguity rule alone; `violations` by `layers` alone, one `{file, line, policy, layer, fragment, text}` per violating line. Field names of the blocks this one consumes are not renamed on either side: `gate`, `gate_detail`, `outcome`, `missing_disciplines`, `blocking`, `to_confirm`, `base`, `item`, `rounds`, `commit`, `commit_sha`.

ship-feature-merge.note: Two failures stay distinct: `conflicts` are the paths a content merge put in conflict, `dirty_paths` the paths the merge would touch that the working tree holds uncommitted. On either, `merged` is false and `merge_sha` is null, and the delivery opens `reconcile` instead of aborting.

reconcile.note: The block the reconcile node returns. `merged` is true when the reconciliation landed the merge, with its `merge_sha`; `overlap` names the paths the working tree and the branch change on the same lines — empty when the two sides are disjoint — and it is non-empty exactly when the run stops to ask. `patch` is the path of the artefact that saves the uncommitted work of the working tree; `dirty_paths` the paths the merge would touch that the working tree holds uncommitted; `question` the structured question for the owner when `overlap` is not empty, `null` otherwise; `ok` false when the node could not proceed. `verdict` and the other fields of § architect are not part of it: the node asks the `reconcile` question of the evaluator and reports its own outcome here.

release.note: The block of the promotion node. `released` is false when nothing was promoted — no channels declared, the copy not standing on the development branch, production carrying commits development lacks, or a dirty tree — and `detail` says which. When it is true, `version` is the number the release wrote, `development_sha` the tip of the development branch after the version commit and `production_sha` where production now stands (the same tip: the promotion is a fast-forward), `changelog` the path whose section was written. `ok` is false only when the node could not proceed. It never pushes: `production_sha` is a local ref.

ledger.note: Written only by architect/ledger.mjs, which validates it against this entry before every write. `outcome`, `coverage` and `gate` take the domains of § review-outcome and § gate once set; until their step ran they are null. `cost` holds only the numbers the host reported for each step, never an estimate.

pool.note: The pool registry, written only by architect/pool.mjs, which validates it against this entry before every write. It records who took each slot and how the delivery left it: `in-use` at acquisition, `free` after the merge and cleanup, `blocked` when the delivery stopped without merging — its tree dirty on purpose, or clean on a branch that went into conflict. The measured state is what git says of the slot, a clean tree or a dirty one, and where its commits stand; `state` is the attribution the agent cannot re-derive, and a slot marked `in-use` whose tree is clean is one a run abandoned. Reusability is measured, never read off `state`: a slot is reusable when its tree is clean **and** its branch holds nothing the integration branch lacks.

params.note: These are the keys, not the conditions. `backends.<backend>.base_url` is admitted here and absent on a host's native backend (§7 of contracts/orchestration.md): that conditional absence is not expressible as a list, and it is enforced elsewhere — `hooks/lib/contracts-post-edit.mjs` reads environment.json against it after every write.
